questions.question: Define conservation and explain how it differs from preservation.
questions.expected_answer: Conservation is the careful, wise management and protection of natural resources so that they are used sustainably without being destroyed or wasted (e.g. fishing quotas, controlled harvesting, tourism). Preservation protects an area or species from any human use, keeping it untouched (e.g. strict nature reserves, wilderness). SA conservation combines both; it happens at individual, community, government and international scales; Constitution section 24 gives environmental rights.

questions.question: Explain what biodiversity is and identify the main threats to it in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Biodiversity is the variety of all living things - species, genetic variety and ecosystems. SA is megadiverse (2% of land, about 10% of plant species; nine biomes; Cape Floral Region; many endemics). Threats (HIPPO): habitat loss (farming, mining, cities, plantations); invasive alien species (pines, wattles, eucalyptus, water hyacinth); pollution; population growth and consumption; overexploitation (overfishing, abalone and rhino poaching, overharvesting plants); plus climate change. Extinctions include the quagga and bluebuck.

questions.question: Give environmental, economic, social and cultural reasons for conservation.
questions.expected_answer: Environmental: protect biodiversity, prevent extinction, maintain ecosystem services (clean water, soil, pollination, climate regulation). Economic: tourism jobs, fishing, forestry, farming, medicines and products (rooibos, honeybush), cheaper than repairing damage. Social: health from clean air and water; rural livelihoods (food, firewood, medicinal plants, grazing); wellbeing. Cultural/ethical: heritage and identity (springbok, protea), spiritual connections, responsibility to future generations and other living things.
